title: The $5.7 Million Question: National Money Is Flooding TX-28 — For Tijerina and Against Him
excerpt: Webb County voters deciding the TX-28 congressional race between Henry Cuellar and Tano Tijerina are being outspent, out-shouted, and out-advertised by people who do not live here.
content:
Webb County voters deciding the TX-28 congressional race between Henry Cuellar and Tano Tijerina are being outspent, out-shouted, and out-advertised by people who do not live here. Federal filings and ad-tracking data show outside groups have poured millions into this race on both sides — and the biggest player on Tijerina's side has already started walking away.

The money against him

Independent expenditure filings with the Federal Election Commission through October 20 show roughly $5.7 million spent against Tijerina — led by the House Majority PAC, the Democratic House super PAC, at about $4.6 million, with BOLD America (~$605,000) and CHC BOLD PAC (~$502,000) piling on. House Majority PAC's own filings put its total activity in this race at $4,796,717 through October 22.

The money for him — and the catch

In those same FEC independent-expenditure filings, groups supporting Tijerina total only about $160,000 (No Going Back PAC ~$101,000, America PAC ~$56,000, NRA Victory Fund $2,376). But that number does not tell the whole story. Ad-tracking data reported by the Texas Tribune shows the Congressional Leadership Fund — the Republican super PAC tied to House GOP leadership — had already spent about $4.6 million on ads in this race benefiting Tijerina before it canceled a further $3 million in reserved airtime on October 14. Money already spent is not the same as money still coming — and the canceled $3 million is money Tijerina will never see.

Why the two counts differ

The FEC's own by-candidate totals capture only part of the picture, because much of the fall spending by both super PACs runs through 24- and 48-hour notices rather than the periodic reports the FEC totals are built from, and ad trackers count ads that actually aired while the FEC counts reported obligations. Webb Watch 956 is reporting both sets of numbers so readers can see the full picture instead of a partial one.

The bottom line for Webb County

Roughly $4.6 million in Democratic-aligned outside money has been spent attacking the county judge, and roughly $4.6 million in Republican-aligned outside money was spent backing him — and then his side's biggest backer cut $3 million and headed for the exit with three weeks left. Tijerina's own campaign raised $1.78 million, none of it from his own pocket. When outside groups spend this kind of money in a Laredo race, the question for voters is simple: who are they spending it for — and what do they expect to get back?

Sources:

  • FEC candidate and committee filings for Tano Tijerina (H6TX28124), committees C00929174, C00894543, C00895128
  • FEC independent expenditure filings through October 20–22, 2026
  • Texas Tribune, October 14, 2026, citing AdImpact ad-tracking data
